stories.question: Which variants do these two blood donors carry?

why.route: The question asks for an analysis of the user's own sequenced samples; the router sends that to nextseek_query, whose pipeline agent offers the nf-core run.
why.pipelines: Two human PCR-free whole-genome DNA libraries, so germline SNV, indel and structural-variant calling is sarek. rnavar is wrong because these are DNA, not RNA-seq; methylseq is wrong because nothing was bisulfite converted.

stories.question: I want a VCF of the germline SNVs and indels for each exome.

why.route: The question asks for an analysis of the user's own sequenced samples; the router sends that to nextseek_query, whose pipeline agent offers the nf-core run.
why.pipelines: Human exomes captured with Agilent SureSelect Human All Exon V7: a per-sample germline VCF is sarek's output (with its exome setting and the kit's target BED). rnavar calls variants from RNA-seq only; hlatyping types HLA alleles and does not produce a genome-wide VCF.

stories.question: Run nf-core sarek in tumour-normal mode on this patient's samples.

why.route: The question asks for an analysis of the user's own sequenced samples; the router sends that to nextseek_query, whose pipeline agent offers the nf-core run.
why.pipelines: One patient with a colon tumour and a matched blood normal, both WGS and both linked to the patient, which is what sarek's somatic tumour-normal calling needs. rnavar would be wrong: these are DNA libraries. must_match is left empty because the template's default tools (haplotypecaller, manta) hold no somatic caller; a good launch adds one (strelka or mutect2), so rule whether to require it.
